ranges.toolingNote: tools/plan/generate.js currently raises inline string codes MET-T001..MET-T030 (see its header comment) and is NOT wired to this registry — it runs before code.json/data/errors.json can be trusted to exist. Migrating it to read data/errors.json (or a generated tooling subset) is future work; do not remove or renumber its inline codes without updating this note and the script together.

MET-F001.message: error registry failed to load from {path}: {cause}
MET-F001.remedy: Check that data/errors.json exists, is valid JSON, and passes schema validation (unique codes, required fields, MET-<layer><NNN> format). Set METROPOLIS_ERRORS_PATH to override the resolved path if it was found in the wrong place.

MET-F002.remedy: Fix the offending entry in data/errors.json (duplicate code, bad code format, or missing severity/module/message/remedy field) and reload.

MET-F003.remedy: Add {code} to data/errors.json before using it — GR#7 forbids ad-hoc error construction. This wrapper error is itself always available even if the registry failed to load, so the failure is never silent.

MET-F004.message: correlation ID missing or empty when constructing error {code}
MET-F004.remedy: Every errs.New/errs.Wrap call must carry a non-empty correlation ID. Mint one with errs.NewCorrelationID() at the boundary (protocol command, CLI invocation, test setup) and propagate it through the call chain.

MET-F010.message: failed to write NDJSON log entry to {path}: {cause}
MET-F010.remedy: Check disk space and file permissions on the logs/ directory. The error is still retained in the in-memory ring buffer (Recent()) even when the write fails.

MET-F011.remedy: Check that logs/ is writable and that rotated files (.1, .2, .3) are not locked by another process. Logging continues to the current file uncapped until rotation succeeds.

MET-F012.message: cannot open log file {path} for writing: {cause}
MET-F012.remedy: Ensure the logs/ directory exists and is writable, or set an explicit writer via NewLogger. Falls back to the in-memory ring buffer sink so errors are never printed-and-lost.

MET-F013.message: malformed log entry could not be marshalled to JSON: {cause}
MET-F013.remedy: Ensure ctx values passed to errs.New/Wrap are JSON-marshalable (no channels, funcs, or cyclic structures).

MET-F020.remedy: Correlation IDs must be UUIDv4-formatted strings minted by errs.NewCorrelationID(). Do not hand-construct correlation IDs.

MET-F100.message: module registry: key {key} is already registered
MET-F100.remedy: Register each module key exactly once. There is no re-registration API by design — construct a fresh Registry (one per boot/test) instead of calling Register twice for the same key.

MET-F101.message: module registry: Register called for key {key} with a nil stub
MET-F101.remedy: GR#20 requires every registered module to pair a mandatory stub with its (optional) real implementation. Pass a non-nil Module for stub — real may be nil, stub may not.

MET-F102.message: module registry: key {key} was never registered
MET-F102.remedy: Call Register for {key} before calling Get/UpdateHealth/RecordTickCost/SetStatus/TickCostHistory against it. Check for a typo'd key or a boot-order bug (this module's Register call running after the one that failed).

MET-F103.message: module registry: key {key} does not allow runtime status toggling
MET-F103.remedy: Pass registry.WithCanToggle(true) when registering {key} if the F12 UI should be able to toggle its status; toggling is opt-in, never inferred, so an entry registered without it always rejects SetStatus.

MET-F104.message: module registry: SetStatus for key {key} was called with a missing or mismatched confirm token
MET-F104.remedy: Pass confirmToken equal to the exact module key being toggled (the confirm-token pattern the F12 UI satisfies by having the user re-confirm the key). A blank or wrong token is refused rather than silently ignored.

MET-F105.message: module registry: key {key} cannot move to status:real — no real implementation was registered for it
MET-F105.remedy: Pass a non-nil real Module to Register for {key} (or via a future re-registration path) before requesting StatusReal, either at registration (WithStatus(StatusReal)) or via SetStatus.

MET-F106.message: module registry: method called on a struct copy of the Registry NewRegistry returned
MET-F106.remedy: SEC-020: never dereference-and-copy a *Registry ('r2 := *r'). Pass the *Registry pointer NewRegistry gave you (or that a caller received from it); a copy carries its own independent mutex over the SAME aliased modules map and is rejected outright rather than allowed to corrupt shared state.

MET-F200.message: shard index {shard} is out of range
MET-F200.remedy: Every ShardResult/Message must carry a Shard index in [0, NumShards). Check the sharding function that produced this result for an off-by-one or a stale NumShards value.

MET-F201.message: shard merge incomplete: got {got} shard results, want {want}
MET-F201.remedy: MergeInOrder requires exactly NumShards results, one per shard, before it will merge deterministically. Check the caller's shard-fan-out loop for a shard that failed to report (e.g. a goroutine that panicked or returned early) rather than let the merge proceed on partial data.

MET-F202.remedy: MergeInOrder requires exactly one result per shard index. Check the caller's shard-fan-out loop for a shard index computed twice (e.g. a modulo bug) rather than merge two results for the same shard, which would make the merge order-dependent and break determinism.

MET-F220.remedy: The requested Micropounds add/sub/mulrat operation would overflow int64 (or divide by zero, for mulrat). This is reported rather than silently wrapped or truncated so money never drifts (AC-11) — check the calling code for an unreasonably large input rather than retry with the same values.

MET-F300.message: BinarySerializer method not implemented for shard {name}
MET-F300.remedy: BinarySerializer is a reserved-but-unbuilt StateSerializer (A3: arrives only when profiling shows JSON marshalling is the amortised cold-pass bottleneck at 100M-citizen scale). Use NDJSONSerializer, the canonical serializer for every save/fixture/config/protocol-debug shard today, instead.

MET-F301.message: shard name {name} is not a valid single path component; rejected to prevent path traversal / zip-slip (SEC-001)
MET-F301.remedy: A ShardMeta.Name decoded from a bundle's header.json is untrusted input, not a trusted local value — it must be a single clean path component with no separators, drive/volume markers, or '.'/'..' segments. This bundle's header.json claims a shard name that fails that check; treat the bundle as hostile or corrupt rather than trying to sanitise the name into something plausible. If this fires on a bundle you trust, the name itself (not this check) is the bug — fix whatever produced header.json.

MET-F400.message: solver Registry method called on a struct-copied Registry value (correlation {correlationId})
MET-F400.remedy: Registry (internal/foundation/solver) must be constructed via NewRegistry and used through that same pointer for its whole lifetime — never dereferenced-and-copied ('r2 := *r'). A copy gets its own, independent mutex while its registrations slice still aliases the original's, and the copy's own next lock attempt can hang forever if it was taken mid-lock on the original (SEC-020/SEC-016). Fix the call site to hold and pass the original *Registry, not a copied value.

MET-F600.message: data/ directory could not be resolved (checked ${env}, executable-relative search, and working-directory-upward search)
MET-F600.remedy: Set METROPOLIS_DATA_DIR to the repo's data/ directory explicitly, or run from within (or below) the repo so the upward search can find it. The search requires one of the known §24 config files (e.g. consumption.json) to actually be present, not just a directory named data.

MET-F601.remedy: Check that the resolved data directory contains the expected §24 file, and that ResolveDataDir found the correct directory (see MET-F600's search order).

MET-F602.message: config file at {path} is not well-formed JSON: {cause}
MET-F602.remedy: Fix the JSON syntax error at {path}. Check the underlying cause for the line/column the decoder stopped at.

MET-F603.message: config file at {path} is missing a valid top-level "version" field
MET-F603.remedy: Every §24 config file must declare a positive integer "version" field. Add or correct it at {path}.

MET-F604.message: config file at {path} failed schema validation: field {field}: {rule}
MET-F604.remedy: Fix the named field at {path} per the reported rule (required/type/range check) in the file's Validate() implementation.

MET-F605.message: Reload for {path} was requested while debug mode is disabled
MET-F605.remedy: Hot-reload of config files is gated on debug mode (feat.debugmode) being enabled on the Store's shared DebugFlag. Enable debug mode via the --debug flag, config, or the :debug on palette command before calling Reload, or wait for the debug console to expose the reload control.

MET-F606.remedy: Check the underlying cause (malformed JSON, missing version, schema violation — see MET-F601-F604) and fix the file at {path}. The previously-loaded config remains live and unaffected until a Reload succeeds (AC-11).

MET-F607.message: buildings.json entry {field} references a consumption class that consumption.json does not define
MET-F607.remedy: Either add the missing class to data/consumption.json's "classes" map (engine.consumption/MOD-021's own balance data), or fix the offending buildings.json entry's consumptionRef to name an existing class key. See FEAT-010/data.catalogue AC-12.

MET-F608.message: Get/OnChange/Reload for {path} called on a copied Store value, not the one NewStore constructed
MET-F608.remedy: Always use the *Store[T, PT] pointer NewStore returned. Do not dereference-and-reassign it ('s2 := *s1') or pass it by value -- that produces a second Store value with its own reloadMu/cbMu but an aliased cbs backing array, defeating this package's concurrency-safety invariant (BUG-125/SEC-020). If you need a second independent Store, call NewStore again.

MET-F700.message: astgate failed to parse source file {path}: {cause}
MET-F700.remedy: Fix the syntax error in {path} (a go/parser error surfaced while astgate's AST walk, BUG-024, was scanning cmd/ or internal/ for copy-guard candidates) — the file must be valid Go for go build/go vet/astgate to all succeed. If {path} is intentionally malformed (a fixture), it belongs under a _test.go-adjacent tree astgate excludes, not a scanned production path.

MET-F701.remedy: Check that {root} exists and is readable — this wraps a filepath.WalkDir failure (missing directory, permission error) astgate hit while scanning for BUG-024's copy-guard candidates. astgate cannot produce a trustworthy result from a partial walk.

MET-F702.message: astgate could not find go.mod walking upward from {dir}
MET-F702.remedy: Run astgate (directly, or via go test ./... in the build-test-vet CI job) from within the repository, or below its root, so resolveRepoRoot's upward search can find go.mod. If this fires in CI, check the working directory the job invoked the gate from.

MET-F703.message: astgate found two distinct violations with the identical ratchet key {key}: {firstLocation} and {secondLocation}
MET-F703.remedy: BUG-119 round 6/7's structural fix (Bill's ruling): violationKey must be derived from each node's complete identity (file + full enclosing declaration chain + kind + the full type expression as printed), and building the key map is REQUIRED to hard-fail on any two distinct nodes producing the same key -- a silent merge is exactly how rounds 1-5 shipped incomplete keys. This means violationKey itself is still missing something that distinguishes these two real, different findings. Do not special-case this pair -- find and fix the remaining gap in violationKey's identity tuple (or the printer/type-expression logic feeding it), then re-run. Never suppress this error by removing one of the findings from the ratchet map.

MET-F704.message: astgate failed to open accepted-findings registry {path}: {cause}
MET-F704.remedy: SEC-048: LoadAcceptedFindings' opening read of the checked-in accepted-findings.json (BUG-024's ratchet allowlist) failed for a reason other than the file simply not existing (a missing file is not an error -- see LoadAcceptedFindings' doc comment). Check that {path} is readable and not a directory; if the file was deliberately removed, that is a no-op (empty registry), not a fix for this error.

MET-F705.message: astgate could not parse accepted-findings registry {path} as JSON: {cause}
MET-F705.remedy: SEC-048: the checked-in accepted-findings.json is malformed. This file is the sole evidence the BUG-024 ratchet trusts (ASM-204), so LoadAcceptedFindings fails closed rather than silently treating a corrupt file as an empty registry. Fix the JSON (must be an array of {finding, reason} objects) and re-run.

MET-F706.message: astgate accepted-findings registry {path} entry {index} is incomplete (finding={finding} reason={reason})
MET-F706.remedy: SEC-048: every entry in accepted-findings.json requires both a non-empty "finding" (violationKey's output -- BUG-119) and a non-empty "reason" a human gave for accepting it. Fill in the missing field(s), or remove the entry if it was added by mistake.

MET-F707.message: astgate accepted-findings registry {path} has more than one entry for finding {finding}
MET-F707.remedy: SEC-048: LoadAcceptedFindings refuses to guess which of two entries for the same violationKey is authoritative (fail closed, not silently take-the-last). Remove the duplicate entry from accepted-findings.json, keeping the one reason that should stand.

MET-U001.remedy: Run inside a real terminal (Windows Terminal or conhost) that tcell supports. If running headless (CI, scripts), use core.NewScreen with an injected tcell.SimulationScreen instead of the real terminal constructor. Check TERM/terminfo if this occurs on an unusual terminal emulator.

MET-U002.message: malformed delta for subscription {subscriptionId} at tick {tick} could not be applied: {cause}
MET-U002.remedy: The delta's Patch was not valid JSON (or otherwise failed to apply) and was dropped; the view model for that subscription keeps its last-known-good state. If this persists, check the sending engine module's view-patch encoding for that view.

MET-U003.message: RenderLoop method called on a struct-copied value (BUG-018): {method}
MET-U003.remedy: A *core.RenderLoop value was copied by assignment/passing instead of being used via the single pointer core.NewRenderLoop returned (owned is an atomic.Bool VALUE -- a copy gets its own independent atomic word, so a copy's CAS can succeed even while the original already owns the screen, giving two goroutines that each believe they hold T-RENDER's exclusive tcell.Screen access). The call was rejected rather than risking two writers to one terminal; construct exactly one RenderLoop via NewRenderLoop and pass its pointer everywhere instead of a dereferenced copy.

MET-U100.message: malformed f1.viewport patch could not be applied: {cause}
MET-U100.remedy: The patch was not valid f1.viewport v1 JSON (bad JSON, unrecognised schemaVersion, or a sparse patch received before any full snapshot) and was dropped; the map screen's grid keeps its last-known-good state. If this persists, check the sending engine module's f1.viewport patch encoding (internal/engine/stub/viewport.go documents the v1 schema).

MET-U101.message: MapScreen method called on a struct-copied value (SEC-020): {cause}
MET-U101.remedy: A *mapscreen.MapScreen value was copied by assignment/passing instead of being used via the single pointer mapscreen.NewMapScreen returned (mu is a sync.Mutex VALUE and grid is an aliased slice — a copy is a second, independent lock racing the original over the same backing array). The call was rejected rather than risking a lock-order hang or a torn grid read; construct exactly one MapScreen via NewMapScreen and pass its pointer everywhere instead of a dereferenced copy.

MET-U200.remedy: The module registry has not been wired into the debug screen yet (nil Registry) or has not finished booting. The F12 panel renders an explicit "unavailable" state for this pane rather than a blank panel; no action needed until the registry is constructed and passed to debug.NewScreen.

MET-U201.remedy: The debug screen's error-tail source was explicitly unset (WithErrorTailSource(nil)) or returned no usable data. The F12 panel renders an explicit "unavailable" state for this pane; wire a source (defaults to errs.Recent) to restore it.

MET-U202.remedy: No BoWSource was configured (WithBoWSource) or the configured source's Summary() call failed. The F12 panel renders an explicit "unavailable" state for this pane rather than a blank one; check the metro BOW connection if a source is configured.

MET-U203.message: Screen method called on a struct-copied value (SEC-020): {cause}
MET-U203.remedy: A *debug.Screen value was copied by assignment/passing instead of being used via the single pointer debug.NewScreen returned (mu is a sync.Mutex VALUE and reg/events are aliased pointer/slice fields — a copy is a second, independent lock racing the original over the same referents). The call was rejected rather than risking a lock-order hang or a torn read; construct exactly one Screen via NewScreen and pass its pointer everywhere instead of a dereferenced copy.

MET-U300.message: Register rejected: mnemonic path {path} duplicates an already-registered action at the same path
MET-U300.remedy: Two actions were registered at the identical mnemonic path (AC-14) — key grammar order must never decide which action wins. Pick a distinct mnemonic path for the new action, or remove the earlier Register call for the same path.

MET-U301.message: Register rejected: mnemonic path {path} conflicts with {conflictsWith} — a path cannot be both a complete action and a prefix of another registered path
MET-U301.remedy: ASM-118: the grammar cannot tell, on feeding the shorter path, whether to dispatch immediately or wait for a longer continuation, so this shape is rejected at Register time rather than resolved by a runtime tiebreak. Choose non-overlapping mnemonic paths (e.g. register the leaf under a different top-level token) so no registered path is a strict prefix of another.

MET-U302.message: keymap profile at {path} is malformed or schema-invalid: {cause} — falling back to the shipped default profile
MET-U302.remedy: The profile file was not valid keymap JSON (bad JSON, unrecognised schema version, or the wrong shape). The grammar continues operating on the shipped default profile so the game stays playable; fix the profile file's JSON and reload.

MET-U303.message: keymap entry rejected: physical key {key} maps to mnemonic path {path}, which names no registered action
MET-U303.remedy: A remapped or imported keymap profile bound a physical key to a mnemonic path that this KeyGrammar has no Register()ed action for. That one binding is dropped (AC-11b); the rest of the profile still loads. Register the target action before loading the profile, or fix the profile's path to match a real registered action.

MET-U304.message: command palette argument {name} in {command!q} does not match the expected {kind} form: {value!q}
MET-U304.remedy: The palette's free-text command string is validated per positively-stated argument grammar (AC-9b) before it can influence dispatch; a value outside that grammar is rejected, never silently coerced to zero or truncated. Re-enter the command using the documented form for that argument kind (see doc.go's palette argument grammar table).

MET-U305.message: mark slot {id!q} is not a valid 12-slot mark identifier (a-l)
MET-U305.remedy: Only the 12 mark slots a through l are addressable (AC-7); a 13th distinct identifier is rejected rather than silently overwriting an existing slot. Use one of the 12 documented slots, or clear/reuse an existing one explicitly.

MET-U306.message: Register/RegisterGlobal rejected: token {token!q} is reserved for a built-in binding (Esc/./u/U) and can never be reached through the leader tree or global lookup
MET-U306.remedy: Esc, '.', 'u', and 'U' are unconditionally intercepted by Feed before the leader tree or the global-binding map is ever consulted (see doc.go/grammar.go), so registering an action under one of them would be permanently unreachable dead code. Choose a different mnemonic token or global key.

MET-U307.message: command palette input names unknown command {name!q}
MET-U307.remedy: No RegisterCommand call has registered a palette command with this name. Check the spelling, or register the command before parsing input that references it.

MET-U308.message: KeyGrammar method called on a struct-copied value (SEC-020): {cause}
MET-U308.remedy: A *keys.KeyGrammar value was copied by assignment/passing instead of being used via the single pointer NewKeyGrammar returned (mu is a sync.Mutex VALUE and the trie/usage/marks maps are aliased reference fields — a copy is a second, independent lock racing the original over the same referents). The call was rejected rather than risking a lock-order hang or a torn read; construct exactly one KeyGrammar via NewKeyGrammar and pass its pointer everywhere instead of a dereferenced copy.

MET-E000.message: AdvanceTicks requested with N={n}, must be > 0 and <= {max}
MET-E000.remedy: Send AdvanceTicksPayload.N as a positive integer no greater than MaxAdvanceTicksPerCall. The request is rejected outright rather than clamped to the limit (AC-11) — split it into multiple calls if you need more ticks.

MET-E001.remedy: Check the registered PhaseHook's RunShard implementation named in the correlation ID's log trail for the underlying failure. That phase's barrier still ran for whatever effects were already emitted, but the tick's remaining phases were aborted (AC-10) — fix the hook and re-issue AdvanceTicks.

MET-E002.remedy: Send SetSpeedPayload.Speed as one of the documented multipliers (1, 2, 4; 8x is reserved for feat.debugmode and rejected here when debug is off).

MET-E003.message: Subscribe requested with malformed view name {view}: {cause}
MET-E003.remedy: Send SubscribePayload.ViewName in the documented naming scheme (protocol.ValidateViewName). Check the underlying cause for the specific rule violated.

MET-E004.remedy: engine.core v1 serves exactly one view, "engine.status". Request that view name, or wait for the view you need to land.

MET-E005.remedy: Only unsubscribe a subscription ID previously returned by a successful Subscribe call. This subscription may already have been unsubscribed, or never existed on this engine instance.

MET-E006.remedy: Check the caller-supplied io.Writer for Snapshot (disk space, permissions, or a closed writer) — the underlying cause names the specific failure from the NDJSON shard-write step.

MET-E007.message: RegisterPhaseHook called for phase {phase} with a nil hook
MET-E007.remedy: Pass a non-nil PhaseHook to RegisterPhaseHook. A nil hook is rejected rather than silently skipped during phase execution.

MET-E008.remedy: Pass a PhaseKind present in DailyPhaseOrder or MonthlyPhaseOrder. Check for a typo'd or stale phase constant.

MET-E009.remedy: This should be unreachable in practice: protocol.Command.Validate's commandRegistry already closes the Kind<->payload mapping before a command reaches HandleCommand. If seen, a new protocol.CommandKind was added without a matching case in engine.core's dispatch switch — add one.

MET-E010.message: HandleCommand received an invalid command envelope: {cause}
MET-E010.remedy: This should be unreachable via the normal transport path: protocol.InProcTransport.SendCommand already validates the envelope (ProtocolVersion, CorrelationID, Payload) before enqueueing. If seen, a caller invoked HandleCommand directly with a hand-built Command that skipped that check (e.g. a test, or a future transport) — validate before calling, or fix the transport.

MET-E011.message: RegisterPhaseHook called after the engine sealed (first AdvanceTicks call)
MET-E011.remedy: Register every PhaseHook before the first AdvanceTicks call. There is no hot re-registration API: once AdvanceTicks has run once, the Engine seals its hook set permanently so runPhase's per-tick reads never need to synchronise against a concurrent writer (SEC-003). Construct the Engine, call RegisterPhaseHook for every hook, then start advancing ticks.

MET-E012.message: RegisterPhaseHook/AdvanceTicks called on a copied Engine value, not the one NewEngine constructed
MET-E012.remedy: Always use the *Engine pointer NewEngine returned. Do not dereference-and-reassign it ('e2 := *e') or pass it by value -- that produces a second Engine value with its own mutex and sealed flag but an aliased hooks map, defeating this package's concurrency-safety invariant (SEC-014). If you need a second independent Engine, call NewEngine again.

MET-E013.message: Subscribe/Unsubscribe/PublishEngineStatus called on a copied SubscriptionServer value, not the one NewSubscriptionServer constructed
MET-E013.remedy: Always use the *SubscriptionServer pointer NewSubscriptionServer returned. Do not dereference-and-reassign it ('s2 := *s') or pass it by value -- that produces a second SubscriptionServer value with its own mutex but an aliased subs map, defeating this package's concurrency-safety invariant (SEC-019, same class as SEC-014/016 on Engine). If you need a second independent SubscriptionServer, call NewSubscriptionServer again.

MET-E014.message: RunCommandLoop's CommandSource closed its Commands() channel before ctx was done
MET-E014.remedy: This means the transport went away for some reason other than the shutdown you told RunCommandLoop about (e.g. Close() was called without first cancelling ctx and joining the loop's goroutine). Follow the documented shutdown order: cancel ctx, wait for RunCommandLoop to return, THEN close the transport -- see RunCommandLoop's 'Exit contract' doc comment (internal/engine/core/commands.go) and StubEngine.Run's identical contract (internal/engine/stub/engine.go) for the full ordering argument. A headless run treating this as a silent success would hash a truncated world (engine.headless.md AC-4).

MET-E015.message: SetSpeed(8x) rejected: no Speed8xGate configured on this Engine
MET-E015.remedy: Speed8xDebug is only a valid multiplier once a caller wires an authorising gate via WithSpeed8xGate (normally feat.debugmode.State.AllowSpeed8x) -- an Engine built without one denies Speed8xDebug by default rather than silently permitting it. Wire WithSpeed8xGate(...) when constructing the Engine, or use 1x/2x/4x if debug mode is not intended for this run. Distinct from MET-E002 (ErrInvalidSpeed): that code means the requested speed value itself is out of range, not that a valid 8x request has nowhere to be authorised.

MET-H200.message: -scenario file {path} could not be read or parsed: {cause}
MET-H200.remedy: Check the -scenario path exists, is readable, and contains a well-formed JSON command list. This is checked before the engine boots or any tick advances, so a bad scenario file never produces a partial run.

MET-H201.remedy: Check the -out directory's parent is writable and does not already exist as a stale bundle (CreateBundleDir refuses to overwrite). A write failure here always exits non-zero -- it never silently reports success with no file written.

MET-H202.message: command {kind} rejected by the engine during a headless run: {engineErrorCode}
MET-H202.remedy: The engine rejected a command issued by the headless driver (a scenario-script command, or an internal AdvanceTicks batch) -- see engineErrorCode for the underlying engine.core rejection. This aborts the run rather than silently skipping the rejected command.

MET-H203.message: engine.core.RunCommandLoop exited abnormally during a headless run: {cause}
MET-H203.remedy: A headless run has no operator watching a screen, so a premature engine-loop exit (the transport closing before shutdown was requested -- see engine.core's MET-E014) must never be mistaken for a clean, complete run. Investigate why the transport closed early; do not trust a snapshot file this run may have already written.

MET-E100.message: determinism gate requested with months={months}, must be > 0
MET-E100.remedy: Call RunGate with a positive months value. A gate that runs zero or negative months cannot advance any ticks to compare.

MET-E101.message: determinism gate requested with only {runs} RunSpec(s), need at least 2
MET-E101.remedy: Pass at least two RunSpecs to RunGate. A gate that only ever runs once can never detect a determinism mismatch between runs (AC-9's "a gate that can't fail is no gate", enforced here at construction time rather than left as a design footnote).

MET-E102.message: AdvanceTicks command for run {run} was rejected: {engineErrorCode}
MET-E102.remedy: Check the underlying engine rejection ({engineErrorCode}) for run {run} — this is an infrastructure failure of the command path itself, distinct from a hash mismatch between runs (which is not an error; see GateReport.Verdict).

MET-E103.remedy: Check the underlying cause — json.Marshal of the serialize.Header returned by Engine.Snapshot should be unreachable in practice since Header's fields are all plain JSON-safe types, so this points at a Header field type having changed incompatibly.

MET-E200.message: debug mode is off; {capability} is unreachable until debug is enabled
MET-E200.remedy: Enable debug via the --debug flag, config, or the :debug on palette command before invoking {capability}. This is a deliberate rejection, not a silent no-op — debug-gated capabilities never run partially or invisibly with debug off.

MET-E201.message: cannot enable debug via {source}: no save header configured to sticky-flag
MET-E201.remedy: Wire the active save header via debug.WithHeader before calling Enable. Enabling debug without a header to touch would silently skip the mandatory DebugTouched sticky-flag write (M0-ENG §3), so this is refused rather than treated as a no-op.

MET-E202.message: enabling debug via {source} failed: the sticky DebugTouched flag did not persist to the save header: {cause}
MET-E202.remedy: Check the save header write path (foundation.serialize / the caller's PersistFunc) for the underlying cause. Debug enable is refused rather than reporting success with an unpersisted sticky flag, per M0-ENG §3's balance-data hygiene contract.

MET-E203.remedy: Enable debug via one of the defined EnableSource values (flag, config, palette) — this should be unreachable outside a caller bug; check the call site.

MET-E204.message: cheat {kind} was invoked with no effect callback configured
MET-E204.remedy: Wire a non-nil debug.CheatEffect for {kind} before invoking InvokeCheat — this package never applies a cheat's domain effect itself (e.g. engine.finance owns free money/instant build, engine.unlocks owns force milestone).

MET-E205.remedy: Check the injected CheatEffect implementation for {kind} (the owning domain module) for the underlying failure. The cheat is not recorded as used when its effect fails.

MET-E206.message: entity inspector has no lookup configured for ref {ref}
MET-E206.remedy: Wire debug.WithEntityLookup at State construction before calling InspectEntity.

MET-E207.remedy: Check the injected EntityLookup implementation for the underlying failure resolving {ref}.

MET-E208.message: entity inspector could not marshal {ref} to JSON: {cause}
MET-E208.remedy: Ensure the entity type returned by EntityLookup is JSON-marshalable (no channels, funcs, or cyclic structures).

MET-E209.message: fidelity dial has no implementation configured
MET-E209.remedy: Wire debug.WithFidelityDial at State construction before calling FidelityDial.

MET-E210.remedy: Informational audit entry (balance-data hygiene, M0-ENG §3): a debug cheat was invoked successfully. No action required unless unexpected in a shared/demo save; cross-check against the save header's DebugTouched flag and State.CheatLog().

MET-E211.message: debug.State method {method} was called on a struct-copied State, not the value NewState returned; the call was rejected before touching any shared field
MET-E211.remedy: Never copy a *debug.State value (`s2 := *s` or equivalent) — mu is an independent lock on the copy while header/cheatLog remain aliased with the original, so a copy is a second, uncoordinated lock domain over the SAME save header's sticky DebugTouched hygiene flag (SEC-020 wave 2). Always pass and store the *debug.State pointer NewState gave you.

MET-E212.message: cannot submit debug feedback: no feedback inbox directory configured
MET-E212.remedy: Wire the feedback inbox directory via debug.WithFeedbackInbox before calling SubmitFeedback (FEAT-065 AC-DM8) — there is no invented default path; the inbox location is a deployment/config concern the caller owns.

MET-E213.message: debug feedback inbox directory {inbox} could not be created or written: {cause}
MET-E213.remedy: Check the configured feedback inbox path's permissions and that no non-directory file already occupies it. FEAT-065 AC-DM8's file-drop mechanism requires a writable directory before any submission can be durably recorded.

MET-E214.message: debug feedback record could not be written to {path}: {cause}
MET-E214.remedy: Check disk space and permissions on the feedback inbox directory. SubmitFeedback writes via a temp-file-then-rename (never appends, never overwrites) so a partial write here never leaves a half-written record visible to claude-devfeedback-import.js — but the submission itself was not durably recorded and should be retried.

MET-E215.message: debug feedback record could not be marshalled to JSON: {cause}
MET-E215.remedy: Defensive-only: every FeedbackRecord field is a plain string/int64/bool. If this fires, a recent change to FeedbackRecord's fields likely introduced an unmarshalable type — fix the field type rather than working around this at the call site.

MET-U400.message: dev console cannot open: no RequireConsole gate wired at construction
MET-U400.remedy: Construct the Console with WithRequireConsole(state.RequireConsole) before calling Open. This is a construction-time misconfiguration — a genuine gate denial (debug off) is returned unwrapped as feat.debugmode's own ErrDebugRequired (MET-E200), never this code (FEAT-065 AC-DM1's 'not a devconsole-local error code' requirement).

MET-U401.message: dev console action {action!q} attempted before the console was open
MET-U401.remedy: Call Console.Open successfully (which itself gates on debug.State.RequireConsole) before invoking Inspect or SubmitFeedback — FEAT-065 AC-DM7 requires every devconsole surface to be unreachable without first passing through the same gate the console's own open-action uses.

MET-U402.message: dev console capability {capability!q} has no implementation wired
MET-U402.remedy: The Console was constructed without the matching Option (e.g. WithInspect, WithSubmitFeedback, WithPause) for this capability. Wire every capability the caller intends to expose at construction time — an unwired optional seam is refused explicitly rather than silently doing nothing.

MET-U500.message: malformed {view} patch could not be applied: {cause}
MET-U500.remedy: The patch was not valid JSON for the named f6.* view schema (bad JSON, unrecognised schemaVersion, or an oversized payload) and was dropped; the demo screen's affected view keeps its last-known-good state (SF-7/DEMO-9). If this persists, check the sending engine module's view patch encoding for the named view.

MET-U501.message: delta for unknown or stale subscription {subscriptionId} dropped
MET-U501.remedy: ApplyDelta received a protocol.Delta whose SubscriptionID was never bound via BindSubscription (or was bound to a view since unsubscribed). This is expected transiently around resubscribe/unsubscribe races; if it persists, check the caller's SubscriptionID-to-view routing (SF-7/DEMO-9 — never applied, never a panic).

MET-U502.message: Subscribe called with unrecognised view name {view}
MET-U502.remedy: This screen only subscribes to its four registered f6.* views (f6.population, f6.leisure, f6.housing, f6.commute). Passing any other name is a programming error at the call site — fix the caller rather than adding a new view name here without updating code.json's outbound edges and this package's doc.go.

MET-U503.message: method {method} called on a struct-copied Screen (not the *Screen New returned)
MET-U503.remedy: A *demo.Screen value was copied (`s2 := *s`) and a method was then called on the copy. Screen's mu is a sync.Mutex VALUE while subs/stale/typologies/ageMonths/personality/hoursByActivity/leisureTaste/typologyOrder are reference types a copy ALIASES, so a copy is a second, independent lock over state meant to be exclusively owned by the original (SEC-020) — this call is rejected fail-closed instead of racing or corrupting the shared maps/slices. Fix the caller to hold and pass the single *Screen New returned, never a dereferenced copy of it.

MET-E300.message: conservation violated: {invariant} at tick {tick}, expected delta {expected}, actual delta {actual}
MET-E300.remedy: A registered conserved stock's tracked flows (births/deaths/migration, income/expenditure, production/consumption, spawn/despawn) do not explain its actual change for the tick — trace the invariant named here and the tick number to find which module let state drift untracked. In a dev build this is also a hard assert (panic); in a release build this logged error is the only signal, so treat it as P0 (GR#21).

MET-E301.message: invariant.Wire/WireDaily called against phase {phase} after the target engine.core.Engine already sealed
MET-E301.remedy: Wire/WireDaily must be called before the target Engine's first AdvanceTicks call — RegisterPhaseHook rejects late registration (core.ErrEngineSealed, MET-E011) once sealed, and this wrapper surfaces that cause rather than swallowing it. Fix the boot sequence so invariant wiring runs before the first AdvanceTicks call.

MET-E302.message: Registry method called on a copied value, not the one NewRegistry constructed
MET-E302.remedy: Always use the *invariant.Registry pointer NewRegistry returned. Do not dereference-and-reassign it ('r2 := *r') or pass it by value -- that produces a second Registry value with its own mu but ALIASED invariants/names, so the copy's mu protects nothing shared and a copy taken while the original's mu was held can hang the copy's own Lock() forever (SEC-014/SEC-016/SEC-020-class). If you need a second independent Registry, call NewRegistry again.

MET-E303.message: Registry.Register called with a nil Invariant
MET-E303.remedy: Pass a non-nil value implementing the Invariant interface (Name/Check) to Registry.Register.

MET-E304.message: Registry.Register called twice with invariant name {name}
MET-E304.remedy: Every registered Invariant's Name() must be unique within a Registry — this mirrors foundation.registry.Register's duplicate-key rejection. Give the second invariant a distinct name, or confirm it is not an accidental double-registration.

MET-E400.message: OS Terrain 50 import of tile {tile} failed checksum/format validation: {cause}
MET-E400.remedy: The source ASCII-grid/GML tile at {tile} did not pass the importer's header/post-count/checksum check (data/georef.json's source.formats). Re-download the tile from https://osdatahub.os.uk/downloads/open/Terrain50 and re-run the build-time import — the importer never falls back to a silent best-effort partial grid (GR#7).

MET-E401.message: georef.json anchor {anchor} at (E={easting}, N={northing}) resolves outside the downloaded Terrain 50 tile {tile}'s extent [{minE}-{maxE}, {minN}-{maxN}]
MET-E401.remedy: data/georef.json's anchor coordinates must fall inside the actual downloaded tile they claim to sit in. Either the anchor is wrong (re-verify against real OSTN15-transformed data, see georef.json's openQuestions) or the wrong tile was downloaded for this anchor. This is a data-integrity stop, not a best-effort clamp.

MET-E402.message: mutation command against cell/tile {tile} rejected: caller does not own it
MET-E402.remedy: ApplyOwnershipCommand/other mutation commands only succeed against a tile the caller already owns. Purchase the tile first via PurchaseTile, or check TileAt's Owned flag before issuing the command.

MET-E403.message: mutation command against tile {tile} rejected: tile does not exist (outside the {sizeKm}km expansion extent)
MET-E403.remedy: The referenced TileCoord falls outside data/georef.json's expansion box (30x30 tiles at 2km each). Check the coordinate against WorldAPI's extent before issuing the command.

MET-E404.remedy: Either the tile is already owned (re-purchase is a no-op error, not silently accepted twice) or the tile coordinate is out of the expansion extent. See {cause} for which.

MET-E405.message: geology query for tile {tile} rejected: tile has not been prospected
MET-E405.remedy: Mining-relevant geology (clay/gravel/deep-coal presence) is only queryable after Prospect(tile) has run — chalk baseline is always visible, but the fine-grained layer is deliberately gated (§32) so mining siting requires the survey action, not omniscience. Call Prospect first.

MET-E406.message: operation on World value that is not the one NewWorld constructed (a struct copy)
MET-E406.remedy: BUG-064: World embeds its mutex-guarded state by value, mirroring engine.core's Engine. A struct copy (`cp := *w`) gets its OWN, independently-zeroed mu but ALIASES the original's tiles map, defeating mutual exclusion. Every WorldAPI method and every mu-guarded internal helper (ensureTile, tilePrice) rejects a copy with this code, before its own mu is ever touched, exactly as engine.core.Engine's checkNotCopied/ErrEngineCopied does for the analogous SEC-014/SEC-016 hazard. Always call methods on the original *World/*WorldAPI NewWorld/NewWorldAPI returned, never on a dereferenced copy.

MET-E500.remedy: Check the underlying foundation.data error (wrapped, see {cause}) — usually a missing data/ directory, malformed JSON, a curve with other than 12 month points, or a negative multiplier. Fix data/seasonal.json (or its resolution path) and reload; engine.season never falls back to a silent default-to-1.0 curve (GR#15/GR#7).

MET-E501.remedy: engine.season requires all eight §9/§17 curves (electricityWinterPeak, waterSummerPeak, gasSeasonal, harvestCalendar, constructionSpeedMultiplier, schoolIntakeGate, leisureBeachWeight, leisureIndoorWeight, healthWaveModifier) to be present in data/seasonal.json's "curves" map. Add the named curve — foundation.data's schema validation does not catch this because it has no notion of which curve names a particular consumer requires.

MET-E502.message: seasonal curve query rejected: month index {monthIndex} is negative (before the world's epoch)
MET-E502.remedy: Pass a month index >= 0 (engine.core's Clock.Month(), 0 = world genesis). engine.season's curve functions have no defined value before genesis and return this error rather than a negative-modulo wraparound or a panic.

MET-E503.message: internal error: curve "{curve}" not found in a loaded SeasonAPI (Load's completeness check should have caught this)
MET-E503.remedy: This should be unreachable — Load verifies every required curve is present before returning a usable *SeasonAPI, and the curve map is never mutated afterward. If this fires, it's an engine.season bug (a query method referencing a curve name Load's requiredCurves list doesn't cover); file a BUG item, do not treat the returned value as trustworthy.

MET-E504.message: data/seasonal.json's "{curve}" curve has {qualifying} month(s) >= threshold {threshold}, want exactly 1
MET-E504.remedy: The school-intake gate (BUG-059) must have exactly one calendar month at or above schoolIntakeGateThreshold — it is consumed as a once-per-year boolean trigger (engine.education's stage-transition gate), not a continuous multiplier. Fix data/seasonal.json's schoolIntakeGate curve so exactly one month qualifies (typically the single month meant to be September under the file's meta.monthIndexConvention); zero qualifying months means intake silently never fires, two or more means it silently double-fires.

MET-E600.message: data/market.json could not be loaded or failed schema validation: {cause}
MET-E600.remedy: Check data/market.json exists, is valid JSON, has a positive "version", a "pricingMode" of exactly "static" (v1 supports no other mode), and every commodity entry has a recognised supplyMode, a non-empty unit, a non-negative capacityCeiling, and exactly one of importPriceMicropounds (every commodity except waste) or exportPriceMicropounds (waste only) — never both, never neither. engine.market never falls back to a silent default-to-zero or default-to-hybrid substitution (GR#15/GR#7).

MET-E601.remedy: engine.market requires all nine §6/§17/§2.2 commodities (water, power, gas, foodStaples, foodFresh, fuel, constructionMaterials, consumerGoods, waste) to be present in data/market.json's "commodities" map. Add the named commodity — this package's per-entry schema validation does not catch this because it has no notion of which commodity keys this consumer needs.

MET-E602.remedy: Query MarketAPI only with one of the nine registered CommodityType constants (Water, Power, Gas, FoodStaples, FoodFresh, Fuel, ConstructionMaterials, ConsumerGoods, Waste). §10 non-tradable services (education, healthcare, elder care, fire, police, deathcare, leisure, transport) are never registered commodities — this is the expected not-found result for a service name, not a bug.

MET-E603.message: Price() rejected commodity "{commodity}": waste is priced only via ExportPrice
MET-E603.remedy: Waste is §6's negative commodity — the city pays to export it, never pays a supplier to receive it. Call MarketAPI.ExportPrice(Waste) instead of Price(Waste).

MET-E604.message: ExportPrice() rejected commodity "{commodity}": only waste is exported
MET-E604.remedy: ExportPrice exists only for Waste (§6's negative commodity). Call MarketAPI.Price for any other commodity's import price.

MET-E605.message: internal error: commodity "{commodity}" record is missing required field "{field}" despite passing Load validation
MET-E605.remedy: This should be unreachable — Load's foundation/data.MarketFile.Validate and validateCommodityPricingXOR both enforce this field's presence before a *MarketAPI is ever returned, and the commodity map is never mutated afterward. If this fires, either that validation was weakened by a later edit, or a *MarketAPI was constructed by a path that bypasses Load (e.g. a hand-built test fixture); file a BUG item, do not treat the returned MarketAPI as trustworthy.

MET-E700.remedy: Every Registrant must return a stable, non-empty ActionTaxonomyID from its taxonomy-id accessor (AC-1a). Give the registrant's TaxonomyID() a real, unique identifier before registering it.

MET-E701.remedy: Each ActionTaxonomyID may register at most once with a given *Registry (AC-1a: "registry-unique identifier"). Give the new Registrant a distinct taxonomy id, or fix the caller registering the same id twice.

MET-E702.message: Registry.Register called on ActionTaxonomyID "{actionID}" after the registry was sealed
MET-E702.remedy: Registry.Register is boot-wiring-only (AC-3): once Recommend/Preview has read from the registry (or Seal was called explicitly), no further registration is accepted, so a live query never sees a stale view of a registry a later Register mutated underneath it. Move this registration earlier in boot wiring, before the first Recommend/Preview/Seal call.

MET-E703.remedy: Preview only accepts an ActionTaxonomyID that a Registrant has already registered with this *Registry (AC-8, mirrors MarketAPI.lookup's ErrUnknownCommodity precedent). Check the id against Registry.Recommend's candidate set, or register the missing Registrant at boot.

MET-E704.message: precondition "{preconditionID}" could not be evaluated against the given GameStateView: {cause}
MET-E704.remedy: A Precondition's Evaluate must return a registry-sourced error (never a silent false) when it genuinely cannot evaluate — e.g. a required GameStateView field is absent (AC-2). Supply a GameStateView carrying every field the named precondition needs, or fix the precondition to declare its required fields more precisely.

MET-E705.remedy: The caller constructed a GameStateView without a field a registered Precondition or ProjectConsequence query needs (AC-2/AC-8). Populate the field before calling Recommend/Preview, or check the failing precondition/registrant's documented required-field list.

MET-E800.message: save rejected: another save is already in flight for bundle "{finalDir}"
MET-E800.remedy: AC-11's single-save-in-flight guard rejects a second SaveManual/Autosave/Milestone trigger while one is already running on the same Manager, rather than queuing it or letting the two interleave shard writes. Wait for the in-flight save to complete (or fail) before retrying, or use a separate Manager instance if truly concurrent saves to different roots are intended.

MET-E801.message: could not create the staging bundle directory under "{root}": {cause}
MET-E801.remedy: Check filesystem permissions and free space on the save root's volume. No shard has been written yet at this point -- nothing under the discoverable save tree (manual/autosave/milestone) is affected.

MET-E802.message: writing shard for participant kind "{kind}" failed: {cause}
MET-E802.remedy: A registered Participant's RecordSource returned an error, or the underlying shard write/close failed. The staged bundle is discarded (AC-9) -- no already-promoted save (manual, autosave, or milestone) is affected. Check the failing participant's Source implementation and the target filesystem.

MET-E803.message: writing the staged bundle's header.json failed: {cause}
MET-E803.remedy: Check filesystem permissions on the staging directory. The staged bundle is discarded; nothing already-promoted is affected.

MET-E804.message: writing the staged bundle's save-meta.json sidecar failed: {cause}
MET-E804.remedy: Check filesystem permissions on the staging directory. The staged bundle is discarded; nothing already-promoted is affected.

MET-E805.message: staged bundle failed integrity validation before promotion: {cause}
MET-E805.remedy: serialize.ValidateBundle found a problem with the staged bundle (header/shard hash or size mismatch) before this package would have promoted it to a discoverable name (AC-9). The staged bundle is discarded and never becomes selectable via List/Load -- nothing already-promoted is affected. This should be rare; if it recurs, check the participant(s) named in the underlying cause for non-deterministic or malformed record production.

MET-E806.message: promoting the validated staged bundle to "{finalDir}" failed: {cause}
MET-E806.remedy: The bundle passed integrity validation but the final os.Rename into the discoverable save tree failed (e.g. name collision or filesystem error). The staged bundle is deliberately left under root/.staging for forensic inspection rather than deleted. Check the target path and filesystem, then retry the save; clean up the orphaned staging directory once diagnosed.

MET-E807.message: cannot load save at "{dir}": format version is incompatible with this build: {cause}
MET-E807.remedy: The bundle's Header.FormatVersion has a different MAJOR version than this build's serialize.CurrentFormatVersion (AC-12). Newer-major saves require a newer build; older-major saves require a migrator, which does not exist yet (per int.serializer's own documented scope) -- this save cannot be loaded by this build.

MET-E808.remedy: The bundle's save-meta.json sidecar is missing or malformed. If the bundle was written by this package's own Manager, this indicates corruption or an out-of-band edit; check the file directly or restore from an older save.

MET-E809.remedy: The given path does not exist or is not a bundle directory (no header.json). Check the path, or use List to enumerate what actually exists under the save root.

MET-E810.message: no valid autosave could be loaded from "{root}" ({candidates} candidates all failed)
MET-E810.remedy: Every autosave in the rolling-10 history under this root failed to load (corrupted or truncated). Check the returned skip list for the per-entry reasons; if a manual or milestone save exists, load one of those instead via List/Load.

MET-E811.message: could not enumerate save bundles under "{root}" / "{dir}": {cause}
MET-E811.remedy: A filesystem-level failure while listing the manual/autosave/milestone subdirectories under a save root (distinct from a single bundle's header/meta failing to read, which List reports per-entry instead). Check filesystem permissions and that the save root path is correct.

MET-E812.message: save bundle contains shard of kind "{kind}" with no matching registered Participant
MET-E812.remedy: The Manager loading this bundle was constructed with a participant list that does not include a Participant whose Kind() matches this shard -- the registry that wrote the bundle and the one loading it back have drifted apart. Register the missing Participant (or use the same registry the save was written with).

MET-E813.message: reading shard for participant kind "{kind}" failed: {cause}
MET-E813.remedy: A registered Participant's Handler returned an error, or the underlying shard decode failed, while loading a bundle. Check the failing participant's Handler implementation, or (if this bundle is the newest entry in an autosave history) prefer LoadLatest, which skips a corrupted newest entry and loads the next-older valid one instead (AC-10).

MET-E814.remedy: serialize.ValidateBundle rejected this bundle for a reason other than a FormatVersion major mismatch (e.g. a checksum/size mismatch, missing header, a shard path that is a directory instead of a file, or a semantically-bogus header field). Check the wrapped cause for specifics; if this is the newest entry in an autosave history, prefer LoadLatest, which skips a corrupted newest entry and loads the next-older valid one instead (AC-10).

MET-E815.message: reading prior header at "{finalDir}" for save-over debug-touched merge failed: {cause}
MET-E815.remedy: BUG-157: writeBundle detected an existing bundle at finalDir (a save-over of SaveManual/Autosave/Milestone) but could not read its on-disk header.json to carry DebugTouched forward (SEC-024/SEC-027 hygiene). Check the wrapped cause -- a corrupted or hand-edited header.json at finalDir is the most likely culprit; the save is aborted rather than silently risking a debug-touched save coming back clean.

MET-E816.message: manual save name "{name}" is reserved (contains the internal ".replaced-stage-" crash-recovery marker)
MET-E816.remedy: BUG-159: SaveManual rejects any name containing the literal ".replaced-stage-" marker text bundle.go's crash-recovery sibling-detection (BUG-158) uses internally, before any filesystem write. Choose a different manual save name that does not contain this marker text.

MET-E817.message: manual save name "{name}" is unsafe (contains a path separator, drive letter, ".."/"." component, or NUL byte)
MET-E817.remedy: BUG-160: SaveManual rejects any name that is unsafe to join, unmodified, into a save bundle path -- before any filesystem write. Choose a plain manual save name with no '/', '\\', ':', embedded NUL, and that is not empty, ".", or "..".

MET-E818.message: Manager method called on a struct-copied value, not the one NewManager constructed
MET-E818.remedy: Always use the *Manager pointer NewManager returned. Do not dereference-and-reassign it ('m2 := *m') or pass it by value -- that produces a second Manager value with its own independent mu but an ALIASED participants slice, defeating this package's single-save-in-flight guard (SEC-020-class, mirroring Engine.checkNotCopied/Registry.checkNotCopied/Store.checkNotCopied). If you need a second independent Manager, call NewManager again.

MET-E900.message: metropolis failed to boot: {component} failed to initialize: {cause}
MET-E900.remedy: Check the named component ({component}: e.g. tcell screen, harness.stub fixture load, or the module registry) for the underlying cause. cmd/metropolis exits non-zero and never renders a partial/blank screen on this path (AC-7) — rerun with the printed correlation ID to trace the full boot sequence in the log.

MET-P000.message: SendCommand/Close/SendResult/SendEvent/SendDelta/Commands/Results/Events/Deltas called on a copied InProcTransport value, not the one NewInProcTransport constructed
MET-P000.remedy: Always use the *InProcTransport pointer NewInProcTransport returned. Do not dereference-and-reassign it ('t2 := *t') or pass it by value -- that produces a second InProcTransport value with its own closeMu but ALIASED cmdCh/resultCh/eventCh/deltaCh and closeOnce, so the copy's Close() can race the original's in-flight sends and reopen BUG-007's send-on-closed-channel panic (SEC-020 wave 1). If you need a second independent transport, call NewInProcTransport again.

MET-P001.message: Observe/Reset called on a copied SeqTracker value, not the one NewSeqTracker constructed
MET-P001.remedy: Always use the *SeqTracker pointer NewSeqTracker returned. Do not dereference-and-reassign it ('t2 := *t') or pass it by value -- that produces a second SeqTracker value with its own mu but an ALIASED last map, which is a fatal concurrent map access under -race and in production (SEC-020 wave 1, same class as SEC-003/SEC-019). If you need a second independent tracker, call NewSeqTracker again.

MET-P002.message: Allocate called on a copied SubscriptionAllocator value, not the one NewSubscriptionAllocator constructed
MET-P002.remedy: Always use the *SubscriptionAllocator pointer NewSubscriptionAllocator returned. Do not dereference-and-reassign it ('a2 := *a') or pass it by value -- that produces a second, independently-incrementing counter seeded from the same point, so the copy and the original hand out COLLIDING SubscriptionIDs rather than crashing or hanging (SEC-023). If you need a second independent allocator, call NewSubscriptionAllocator again.

MET-P090.remedy: This should be unreachable in practice: every Command reaching StubEngine already passed protocol.DecodeCommand/commandRegistry. If seen, protocol's command vocabulary (commands.go) grew a new Kind without a matching case in StubEngine's dispatch switch — add one.

MET-P091.message: StubEngine rejected command {kind}: payload failed semantic validation
MET-P091.remedy: The command's envelope validated (protocol.Command.Validate) but its payload failed StubEngine's own semantic checks — e.g. AdvanceTicksPayload.N <= 0, an unsupported SetSpeedPayload.Speed, a SubscribePayload.ViewName that fails protocol.ValidateViewName, an UnsubscribePayload for an unknown subscription, or an empty InspectEntityPayload.EntityRef/DebugPayload.Op. Fix the payload's contents before resending.

MET-P092.message: StubEngine.AdvanceTicks requested with N={n}, must be > 0 and <= {max}
MET-P092.remedy: Send AdvanceTicksPayload.N as a positive integer no greater than StubEngine's maxAdvanceTicksPerCall (mirrors engine.core.MaxAdvanceTicksPerCall, SEC-006). The request is rejected outright rather than clamped — split it into multiple calls if you need more ticks. This code is also requested when a well-formed N would overflow the running tick counter (currentTick + n > math.MaxInt64), which the reject leaves unchanged.

MET-P093.message: StubEngine method called on a copied value, not the one NewStubEngine constructed
MET-P093.remedy: Always use the *StubEngine pointer NewStubEngine returned. Do not dereference-and-reassign it ('s2 := *s') or pass it by value -- that produces a second StubEngine value with its own mu but ALIASED subs/rng/transport/world, so the copy's mu protects nothing shared and a copy taken while the original's mu was held can hang the copy's own Lock() forever (SEC-020 wave 2). If you need a second independent StubEngine, call NewStubEngine again.

MET-P094.message: StubEngine.Run: transport Commands() channel closed before ctx was cancelled
MET-P094.remedy: BUG-020: a clean shutdown always cancels Run's ctx before the transport is closed. This error means the transport's command channel closed while ctx was still live -- an unexpected early Close(), a struct-copied transport, or some other bug upstream of Run. Investigate what closed the transport; do not treat this the same as an intentional quit.

MET-H000.message: fixture name {name} is not a valid single path component; rejected to prevent path traversal (SEC-001-class)
MET-H000.remedy: A fixture name is untrusted the moment it could have come from anything other than this build's own record path (a CLI flag, a bug report, a shared directory). It must be a single clean path component, per serialize.ValidateShardName's rule (reused here, not re-derived): no separators, no drive/volume marker, no '.'/'..' segment, no trailing dot or space. Rename the fixture (or fix whatever generated the name) rather than expecting this check to sanitise it.

MET-H001.remedy: Either the fixture's header.FormatVersion major does not match this build's serialize.CurrentFormatVersion major, or its recorded protocolVersion does not match this build's protocol.ProtocolVersion. Regenerate the fixture against this build, or run this build against the fixture's original protocol/format version.

MET-H002.remedy: The fixture's shard bytes failed to decode (bad gzip stream, malformed NDJSON record) or its computed SHA256/size did not match its header's recorded ShardMeta -- treat the fixture as corrupt or tampered rather than trying to load it. Regenerate it from a trusted recording.

MET-H003.message: fixture at {path} could not be read: {cause}
MET-H003.remedy: Check that the fixture's header/shard files exist at the expected path and are readable (permissions, disk state). Distinct from MET-H002: this is an I/O failure, not a decode/integrity failure on bytes that were read successfully.

MET-H004.message: regression replay stopped before every recorded command received a CommandResult: {cause}
MET-H004.remedy: BUG-020-class: ctx was done before EnginePlayer.Replay observed a SendResult callback for every command it sent. Investigate why the target engine's RunCommandLoop stopped consuming/answering mid-sequence rather than treating this the same as a clean, fully-answered replay.

MET-H005.message: Recorder method called on a struct-copied value, not the one NewRecorder constructed
MET-H005.remedy: Always use the *Recorder pointer NewRecorder returned. Do not dereference-and-reassign it ('r2 := *r') or pass it by value -- that produces a second Recorder value with its own mutex but an ALIASED records slice (SEC-020-class). If you need a second independent Recorder, call NewRecorder again.

MET-H006.message: EnginePlayer method called on a struct-copied value, not the one NewEnginePlayer constructed
MET-H006.remedy: Always use the *EnginePlayer pointer NewEnginePlayer returned. Do not dereference-and-reassign it ('p2 := *p') or pass it by value -- that produces a second EnginePlayer value with its own mutex but ALIASED results slice and notify channel (SEC-020-class). If you need a second independent EnginePlayer, call NewEnginePlayer again.

MET-H007.message: fixture shard at {path} exceeded the decompressed-size bound ({maxDecodedBytes} bytes) while reading
MET-H007.remedy: SEC-038: a fixture's decompressed size is bounded during gzip decompression itself (not merely checked after decoding), because a maliciously or accidentally huge compressed shard can decompress to orders of magnitude more memory than its on-disk size suggests. Regenerate a legitimate fixture (which should be small -- a short, deliberately-triggered recording session, not a full save) rather than raising the bound; if a legitimate fixture genuinely needs to be this large, the bound itself (harness/replay's maxFixtureDecodedBytes) needs re-deriving against the new population, not bypassing.

MET-H100.message: key script token {token} at position {position} in script {script} could not be resolved to a key event: {cause}
MET-H100.remedy: A scripted key sequence token must be either a single rune (e.g. "b") or one of the documented <Name> specials (see internal/harness/uitest/doc.go's positively-stated grammar, e.g. <Space>, <Esc>, <Enter>, <Tab>, <F1>..<F12>). Fix the offending token at the reported position — a malformed or unrecognised token is rejected outright, never silently dropped or treated as a literal character (AC-2b), and the same rejection covers a token that names no registered mapping (AC-7).

MET-H101.message: attached harness.replay fixture's Delta stream was exhausted after {got} of the {want} deltas the scripted sequence expected before it ran dry
MET-H101.remedy: The fixture is truncated, corrupt, or was recorded against a different scenario than the script assumes. Regenerate the fixture from a session that actually exercises the scripted sequence's full effects, or lower the expected delta count if the script was over-specified. Never treat this the same as a scenario that completed normally (AC-3b) — a partial buffer must not be snapshotted as if it were the intended final state.

MET-H102.remedy: Run the test with -update to create the golden snapshot from the current output (e.g. `go test ./internal/harness/uitest/... -run <TestName> -update`), then review the generated file before committing it. Distinct from a snapshot mismatch (AC-8) — this fires only when the golden file itself is missing or unreadable.

MET-H103.message: snapshot name {name} (segment {segment}) is not a valid single path component; rejected to prevent path traversal (SEC-001-class)
MET-H103.remedy: A snapshot's file name is derived from t.Name(), split on Go's subtest hierarchy separator ('/'), with every resulting segment validated via serialize.ValidateShardName (AC-5b) — the same function harness.replay's fixture names and ShardMeta.Name are checked with, reused rather than reimplemented. A subtest deliberately or accidentally named ".." (or containing a separator, drive marker, or trailing dot/space) fails this check; rename the subtest rather than expecting this check to sanitise it.

MET-H104.message: Harness method called on a struct-copied value, not the one NewHarness constructed
MET-H104.remedy: Always use the *Harness pointer NewHarness returned. Do not dereference-and-reassign it ('h2 := *h') or pass it by value -- that produces a second Harness value with its own mutex but ALIASED buffers/channels/waitgroup (SEC-020-class, same shape as harness.replay's Recorder/EnginePlayer). If you need a second independent Harness, call NewHarness again.

MET-H105.message: SendCommand rejected: this Transport is a read-only harness.replay fixture playback (AC-3) and never accepts commands
MET-H105.remedy: A fixture attached via Harness.AttachFixture feeds canned Results/Events/Deltas into the view-model layer for snapshot testing (replay.UIPlayer, mode a) — it has nothing to send a command TO. If the test needs to send commands, drive a real (or stub) engine directly instead of attaching a fixture.

MET-H300.message: synthetic citizenCount {citizenCount} is out of range: must be {min}..{max}
MET-H300.remedy: AC-1b: citizenCount sizes real allocation and generation work, so it is validated BEFORE any generation begins and rejected outright rather than clamped. Choose a value between MinSyntheticCitizens and MaxSyntheticCitizens (internal/harness/synth/limits.go) -- the latter reuses foundation.solver's A9 local-CPU ceiling (LocalCitizenCeilingHigh, 30M) rather than an arbitrary number.

MET-H301.message: synthetic sprawl parameter {sprawl} is out of range: must be {min}..{max}
MET-H301.remedy: AC-7b: Sprawl must fall within MinSprawl..MaxSprawl (internal/harness/synth/limits.go, currently 0.0..1.0 inclusive). Rejected outright, never clamped to the nearest legal value.

MET-H302.message: synthetic network shape {networkShape} is not a recognised shape
MET-H302.remedy: AC-7b: NetworkShape must be exactly one of the closed enum values NetworkGrid ("grid"), NetworkRadial ("radial"), or NetworkOrganic ("organic") -- never an arbitrary free string.

MET-H303.remedy: Params passed validation but the underlying write to the caller's io.Writer failed (disk full, closed pipe, permission denied, ...). Check the destination and retry -- this is an I/O failure on a legal request, not a domain-validation rejection (see MET-H300/H301/H302 for those).

MET-H304.message: perf run requested with months={months}, must be > 0
MET-H304.remedy: Call RunPerf (or perfci's -months flag) with a positive months value. A run driving zero or negative simulated months cannot produce a monthly-tick-time measurement.

MET-H305.message: perf run's AdvanceTicks command (n={n}) was rejected by the engine: {engineErrorCode}
MET-H305.remedy: The engine rejected a command issued by RunPerf's tick-driving loop -- see engineErrorCode for the underlying engine.core rejection. The perf run aborts rather than reporting a partial measurement as if it were complete.

MET-H306.message: perf results file {path} is corrupt at line {line}: {cause}
MET-H306.remedy: An existing perf-results NDJSON file failed to parse as the expected PerfRecord schema. This is distinct from AC-8's 'no baseline yet' case (a missing file is never an error) -- a file that exists but will not parse means the results file itself needs investigating (truncated write, manual edit, format drift) before this preset's baseline can be trusted again.

MET-H307.remedy: M0-ENG §6 point 5: a commit that regresses monthly-tick time more than {threshold} (as a fraction) at the 1M-citizen synthetic fails the build. Investigate what the commit changed on the tick path (or, if this is a false positive from a genuinely noisy runner, re-run before concluding the code is at fault -- MinMeasurableDuration's noise floor already screens out near-zero-duration measurements, but does not eliminate all runner variance).

MET-H308.message: perf record rejected: PhaseHookCount/PerfResult provenance not marked as measured
MET-H308.remedy: AppendResult only persists PerfResult values RunPerf itself produced (Measured=true) -- a hand-built PerfResult (e.g. a bare struct literal from a second writer, a hand-edited re-upload) cannot be distinguished from a real measurement once written, so it is rejected before it reaches the results file rather than silently accepted as if RunPerf had produced it (BUG-055). If this is a legitimate new caller, route it through RunPerf, or construct the record via a helper that explicitly sets Measured=true after confirming the figures really came from a real run.

MET-H309.message: perf CI gate could not evaluate this run: {message}
MET-H309.remedy: BUG-071: CompareToBaseline skipped the percentage regression check (ScaleMismatch or BelowNoiseFloor) rather than genuinely passing or failing -- this is NOT a pass. cmd/perfci exits its distinct could-not-evaluate code and does not record this run's measurement as the new baseline. Re-run at a scale/noise level the gate can actually judge (matching CitizenCount/Months against the stored baseline, and comfortably above MinMeasurableDuration) before trusting this commit's perf status either way.

MET-H310.message: perf record for preset {preset} at line {line} is not a plausible genuine measurement: {reason}
MET-H310.remedy: BUG-085: a value like a negative CitizenCount, Months, or PerMonthTick can never be produced by a real RunPerf call (ValidateParams/RunPerf reject these before any measurement begins) -- this record was rejected as untrustworthy provenance even though its Measured flag was set, and LoadLatestBaseline fell back to the last genuinely plausible record. Investigate how this line reached the results file (hand edit, corrupted-cache restore, manual merge-conflict resolution, re-uploaded/edited artifact) -- do not simply re-flip Measured or edit the value to a positive number without understanding how it got there.

MET-H311.message: perf record for preset {preset} sets AcceptedRegression=true with no AcceptedReason
MET-H311.remedy: BUG-083: cmd/perfci's -accept-regression flag (the deliberate, visible way to accept a legitimate slowdown as the new baseline) requires -accept-reason -- a human-readable justification persisted verbatim alongside the accepted measurement. A record claiming an override with no recorded reason is refused as untrustworthy at both the write boundary (AppendResult) and the read boundary (LoadLatestBaseline); re-run cmd/perfci with both flags set to actually accept a regression.

MET-H400.message: could not obtain the weakness-histogram source data: {reason}
MET-H400.remedy: RunWeakness could not exec `node claude-bow.js weakness` or could not parse its stdout into the expected histogram shape. Check node/claude-bow.js are reachable from the repo root, and that its output still matches cmdWeakness's documented shape (claude-bow.js) -- a source that genuinely returned zero findings prints its own known-empty sentinel, which this is NOT that.

MET-H401.message: could not obtain the BOW lint drift report: {reason}
MET-H401.remedy: RunLint could not exec `node claude-bow.js lint` or could not parse its stdout into the expected findings shape. Check node/claude-bow.js are reachable from the repo root, and that its output still matches cmdLint's documented shape.

MET-H402.message: could not obtain sprint {sprint}'s gate status: {reason}
MET-H402.remedy: RunGateStatus could not exec `node claude-bow.js gate-status <sprint>` or could not parse its stdout into the expected per-check/overall shape. Check node/claude-bow.js are reachable from the repo root and that a gate run has actually been recorded for this sprint.

MET-H403.remedy: The perf-results NDJSON file or the accepted-regression registry JSON file existed but could not be parsed cleanly (a torn write, corrupt JSON). This is distinct from the file simply not existing yet, which is not an error -- re-run the perf-CI job or repair/regenerate the named file.

MET-H404.message: failed to write the logged note to the feedback inbox: {path}
MET-H404.remedy: LogNote could not durably write the submitted note (disk error, unwritable inbox directory, marshal failure). The note was NOT filed -- retry the -log command; nothing was silently discarded, but nothing was recorded either until this succeeds.

MET-H405.message: logged note had an empty body
MET-H405.remedy: Pass real note text to -log -- an empty or whitespace-only note is rejected before any file is written, since it would file a useless blank BOW record.
